# ArchaeoMap

> ArchaeoMap is a free, interactive web application that visualizes the historical evolution of human settlements and ancient cities across time — from prehistoric origins to modern metropolises.

For detailed per-city data (rulers, landmarks, populations, founding dates, descriptions, historical alternate names), see [llms-full.txt](https://archaeomap.com/llms-full.txt) — a plain-text dump of every approved city, regenerated automatically from the live database.

For a single city's data in plain text, fetch `https://archaeomap.com/cities/{country-slug}/{city-slug}.txt` (e.g. `/cities/turkiye/bodrum.txt`). The endpoint also accepts historical city-name slugs, so `/cities/turkiye/halicarnassus.txt` returns the same Bodrum entry.

For a hyperlinked HTML directory of every city grouped by country, with each entry annotated by its historical alternate names, see [cities-index.html](https://archaeomap.com/cities-index.html).

## What is ArchaeoMap?

ArchaeoMap lets users explore how cities around the world were founded, grew, changed rulers, built landmarks, and sometimes disappeared — all through an interactive map and timeline slider. It is designed for history enthusiasts, students, researchers, and anyone curious about the ancient world.

The application is accessible at https://archaeomap.com and is completely free to use.

## Core Features

- **Interactive Timeline**: A draggable slider that spans thousands of years. The map updates in real time to show which cities existed during the selected period.
- **City Markers**: Color-coded dots on a world map. Active cities appear in brown, ended cities in dark red, and the selected city is highlighted in gold.
- **City Details Sidebar**: Clicking a city opens a detailed panel showing:
  - Founding date and end date (if applicable)
  - Description of the city's history
  - Historical Control timeline (rulers, empires, dynasties that governed the city)
  - Landmarks history (notable monuments and their construction dates)
  - Population history
- **3D Globe View**: A 3D Cesium-powered globe mode for an immersive perspective.
- **Search and Filter**: Find cities by name or filter by time period.
- **Collections**: Registered users can save cities into personal collections.
- **JSON Export**: Any city's data can be downloaded as a structured JSON file.
- **Responsive Design**: Fully functional on mobile and desktop.

## Data Model

Each city in ArchaeoMap contains:
- `name`: The modern or most recognized name
- `country`: Modern country it belongs to
- `founded`: Year of founding (negative numbers = BCE)
- `endDate`: Year the city ceased to exist (if applicable)
- `coordinates`: Latitude and longitude
- `description`: Historical summary
- `controlHistory`: Array of ruling powers with start/end years and descriptions
- `landmarksHistory`: Array of notable structures with construction dates and purposes
- `populationHistory`: Population estimates over time

## Who Should Use ArchaeoMap?

- History students and teachers looking for visual teaching tools
- Researchers studying urban history, archaeology, or historical geography
- Travelers interested in the ancient origins of cities they visit
- Game developers or writers seeking historical city data
- Anyone curious about how the world looked in 300 BCE, 1000 CE, or any other period

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What time periods does ArchaeoMap cover?**
ArchaeoMap covers cities from prehistoric settlements (thousands of years BCE) through to modern times. The timeline slider allows navigation across this full range.

**Is ArchaeoMap free?**
Yes. ArchaeoMap is completely free to use with no subscription required. An optional account allows saving personal city collections.

**How accurate is the data?**
Data is curated from historical records, archaeological findings, and open-source research. The team continuously improves accuracy. Users and contributors can suggest corrections.

**Can I contribute data?**
Yes. Registered contributors can submit new cities for review. Moderators verify submissions before they appear on the public map.

**Is there an API?**
City data can be exported individually as JSON from the city detail panel. A public API is planned for future development.
